lessons.title: What is Python?
lessons.content: Python is a fun and easy programming language used to build apps, games, and websites.

lessons.question: What can Python be used for?

lessons.title: Why Learn Python?
lessons.content: Python is great for beginners because it’s simple to read and write, like plain English.

lessons.question: Why is Python good for beginners?

lessons.title: Running Python Code
lessons.content: You can write Python code in an editor and run it to see the results.

lessons.question: What do you need to run Python?

lessons.title: Your First Python Code
lessons.content: The print() function shows text on the screen. Example: print('Hello') shows 'Hello'.

lessons.title: Using print()
lessons.content: Use print() with text in quotes, like print('Hi') to display 'Hi'.

lessons.title: Text in Quotes
lessons.content: Text in print() must be in single ('') or double ("") quotes, like 'Hello' or "Hi".

lessons.title: Print 'I love Python' to the screen.
You’re a Python Starter! 🚀
lessons.content: Great job! You’ve started coding with Python. Keep exploring to make cool things!

lessons.title: What is Syntax?
lessons.content: Syntax is the way we write Python code so the computer understands it.

lessons.title: Indentation
lessons.content: Python uses spaces to group code. Usually, we use 4 spaces for indentation.

lessons.question: How many spaces are used for indentation?

lessons.title: Writing Commands
lessons.content: A command like print('Hi') is a single line of code that does something.

lessons.title: Print 'Code is fun' to the screen.
Correct Syntax
lessons.content: Use print() with text in quotes, like print('Wow') to avoid errors.

lessons.question: What happens if syntax is wrong?

lessons.title: Simple Commands
lessons.content: Commands like print('Hello') tell Python what to do, step by step.

lessons.title: Case Sensitivity
lessons.content: Python is case-sensitive, so Print and print are different.

lessons.question: Is PRINT the same as print?

lessons.title: Syntax Star! 🌟
lessons.content: You’re writing Python code like a pro! Keep following the rules to create awesome programs!

lessons.title: What are Comments?
lessons.content: Comments are notes in code that Python ignores. They explain what the code does.

lessons.title: Writing Comments
lessons.content: Use # to start a comment, like # This is a note. It can be on its own line.

lessons.title: Add a comment 'Shows message' above print('Hi').
Comment Placement
lessons.content: Comments can go above code or at the end of a line, like print('Hey') # Note.

lessons.title: Why Use Comments?
lessons.content: Comments help you and others understand your code later.

lessons.title: Add a comment 'Greets user' above print('Hello').
Clear Comments
lessons.content: Write short, clear comments like # Print name to explain the code’s purpose.

lessons.title: Comment Benefits
lessons.content: Good comments make your code easier to fix or share with others.

lessons.title: Comment Champion! 📝
lessons.content: You’re adding helpful notes to your code! Comments make your programs clear and awesome!

lessons.title: What are Variables?
lessons.content: Variables are like boxes that store data, like numbers or text.

lessons.title: Creating Variables
lessons.content: Use = to store a value, like age = 10 or name = 'Mia'.

lessons.title: Create a variable age with value 15.
Variable Names
lessons.content: Variable names should be clear, like score or user, and can’t have spaces.

lessons.title: Using Variables
lessons.content: Use variables in print(), like print(name) to show the stored value.

lessons.title: Create a variable named 'name' with value 'Alex' and print it.
Changing Variables
lessons.content: You can update a variable by assigning a new value, like age = 20.

lessons.title: Variable Power
lessons.content: Variables let you store and reuse data to make programs flexible.

lessons.title: Variable Victory! 📦
lessons.content: You’re storing data like a pro! Variables are your first step to powerful programs!

lessons.title: What are Data Types?
lessons.content: Data types tell Python what kind of data you’re using, like numbers or text.

lessons.title: Integers
lessons.content: Integers are whole numbers, like 5 or 100, used for counting.

lessons.title: Create a variable count with value 8.
Strings
lessons.content: Strings are text in quotes, like 'dog' or "cat", used for messages.

lessons.title: Floats
lessons.content: Floats are numbers with decimals, like 3.14, used for precise measurements.

lessons.title: Create a variable price with value 4.99.
Booleans
lessons.content: Booleans are True or False, used to make decisions in code.

lessons.instruction: Create a variable is_on with True.

lessons.title: Mixing Types
lessons.content: Variables can hold any data type, and you can change the type later.

lessons.title: Data Type Dynamo! 💾
lessons.content: You’re mastering data types! They’re the building blocks of your Python programs!

lessons.title: What are Operators?
lessons.content: Operators let you do math, like adding or multiplying numbers.

lessons.title: Addition
lessons.content: Use + to add numbers, like 5 + 3 equals 8.

lessons.title: Multiplication
lessons.content: Use * to multiply, like 4 * 3 equals 12.

lessons.title: Subtraction
lessons.content: Use - to subtract, like 10 - 4 equals 6.

lessons.title: Division
lessons.content: Use / to divide, like 15 / 5 equals 3.0.

lessons.title: Using Operators
lessons.content: Operators work with variables too, like x = 5; print(x + 2).

lessons.title: Operator Ace! ➕
lessons.content: You’re doing math like a champ! Operators make your code powerful and fun!

lessons.title: What are Strings?
lessons.content: Strings are text, like 'Hello', wrapped in single or double quotes.

lessons.title: Creating Strings
lessons.content: Use quotes to make strings, like message = 'Welcome'.

lessons.title: Create a variable greeting with 'Hello' and print it.
Joining Strings
lessons.content: Use + to combine strings, like 'Hi' + 'there' makes 'Hithere'.

lessons.title: Adding Spaces
lessons.content: To add a space between strings, include ' ', like 'Hi' + ' ' + 'there'.

lessons.title: Print 'Hello' and 'World' with a space between.
New Lines
lessons.content: Use \n to add a new line in a string, like 'Up\nDown'.

lessons.title: String Power
lessons.content: Strings make your programs interactive and expressive.

lessons.title: String Superstar! 📜
lessons.content: You’re crafting text like a wizard! Strings make your programs talkative and fun!

lessons.title: What are Numbers?
lessons.content: Numbers in Python can be integers (like 5) or floats (like 3.14).

lessons.title: Using Integers
lessons.content: Integers are whole numbers, like age = 12, used for counting.

lessons.title: Create a variable score with value 100.
Using Floats
lessons.content: Floats are decimals, like price = 9.99, used for precision.

lessons.title: Math with Numbers
lessons.content: Use numbers with operators, like print(5 + 2) to show 7.

lessons.title: Storing Results
lessons.content: Store math results in variables, like total = 6 + 4.

lessons.title: Number Power
lessons.content: Numbers let you calculate and solve problems in your programs.

lessons.title: Number Ninja! 🔢
lessons.content: You’re crunching numbers like a pro! Keep calculating to build cool stuff!

lessons.title: What is Input?
lessons.content: The input() function lets users type answers, like a question in a game.

lessons.title: Using input()
lessons.content: Use input('Question: ') to ask something, then store the answer.

lessons.title: Ask for a name and say hello.
lessons.expectedAnswer:
name = input('Enter your name: ')
print('Hello ' + name + '!')
blocks:
name = input('Enter your name: ')
print('Hello ' + name + '!')

lessons.title: Storing Input
lessons.content: Save input in a variable, like color = input('Color: ').

lessons.instruction: Ask for a city and store it.

lessons.title: Greeting Users
lessons.content: Combine input with print, like print('Hi, ' + name) to greet users.

lessons.title: Ask for a pet’s name and print 'Pet: ' plus the name.
Input as Text
lessons.content: Input is always text, even if users type numbers.

lessons.title: Interactive Programs
lessons.content: Input makes your programs talk to users and feel alive.

lessons.title: Input Innovator! ⌨️
lessons.content: You’re making programs interactive! User input is your key to fun apps!

lessons.title: What is Type Conversion?
lessons.content: Type conversion changes data types, like turning text into a number.

lessons.title: Text to Number
lessons.content: Use int() to turn text into an integer, like int('5') makes 5.

lessons.title: Convert '10' to an integer and print it.
Converting Input
lessons.content: Input is text, so use int(input()) to get a number from users.

lessons.title: Number to Text
lessons.content: Use str() to turn a number into text, like str(5) makes '5'.

lessons.title: Convert 20 to text and print it with ' years'.
Floats
lessons.content: Use float() to turn text into a decimal, like float('3.14') makes 3.14.

lessons.title: Why Convert?
lessons.content: Conversion lets you do math with input or combine numbers with text.

lessons.title: Conversion Creator! 🔄
lessons.content: You’re changing types like magic! Type conversion makes your code super flexible!

lessons.title: What are Conditionals?
lessons.content: Conditionals let your program make choices, like doing something only if true.

lessons.title: If Statements
lessons.content: Use if to check a condition, like if age > 10: print('Older').

lessons.title: If num = 15, print 'Big' if greater than 10.
Comparisons
lessons.content: Use > (greater), < (less), or == (equal) to compare values.

lessons.instruction: Check if score is equal to 100.

lessons.title: Else Statements
lessons.content: Use else for what happens if the condition is false, like else: print('No').

lessons.title: If x = 5, print 'Small' if less than 10, else 'Large'.
Indentation in If
lessons.content: Indent code under if or else with 4 spaces to show it’s part of the block.

lessons.instruction: Check if age is less than 18.

lessons.question: What runs if the if condition is false?

lessons.title: Smart Choices
lessons.content: Conditionals make your programs decide what to do based on data.

lessons.title: Conditional Captain! ✅
lessons.content: You’re making smart choices with conditionals! Your programs are getting clever!

lessons.title: What is Elif?
lessons.content: Elif means 'else if' and checks another condition if the first if is false.

lessons.title: Using Elif
lessons.content: Use elif after if, like if score > 90: print('A'), elif score > 80: print('B').

lessons.title: If x = 85, print 'B' if >80, else 'C'.
Multiple Elif
lessons.content: You can use multiple elifs to check several conditions in order.

lessons.instruction: Add elif to check if score > 70.
lessons.starterCode:
score = 75
if score > 90:
    print('A')
____ score > 70:
    print('C')

lessons.title: Elif with Else
lessons.content: Use else at the end to cover cases not caught by if or elif.

lessons.title: If x = 60, print 'C' if >80, 'D' if >60, else 'F'.
Elif Order
lessons.content: Python checks elif conditions in order, stopping at the first true one.

lessons.starterCode:
temp = 35
if temp < 20:
    print('Cold')
____ temp > 30:
    print('Hot')

lessons.title: Flexible Choices
lessons.content: Elif lets your program handle many possibilities easily.

lessons.title: Elif Expert! 🌟
lessons.content: You’re mastering multiple choices! Elif makes your programs super smart!

lessons.title: What are Lists?
lessons.content: Lists store multiple items, like fruits = ['apple', 'banana'].

lessons.title: Creating Lists
lessons.content: Use square brackets [], like colors = ['red', 'blue'].

lessons.title: Create a list ['cat', 'dog'] and print it.
Accessing Items
lessons.content: Use index numbers, like list[0] to get the first item.

lessons.question: What is the first index in a list?

lessons.title: List Length
lessons.content: Use len() to count items, like len(['a', 'b']) returns 2.

lessons.title: Changing Lists
lessons.content: Update items with index, like list[0] = 'new'.

lessons.title: List Flexibility
lessons.content: Lists can hold numbers, text, or both, and you can change them.

lessons.title: List Legend! 📋
lessons.content: You’re organizing data with lists! They’re perfect for storing lots of items!

lessons.title: What are Loops?
lessons.content: Loops repeat code, like printing a list of names one by one.

lessons.title: For Loops
lessons.content: For loops go through items, like for fruit in ['apple', 'banana']: print(fruit).

lessons.title: Looping with range()
lessons.content: Use range(3) to loop 3 times, starting from 0: 0, 1, 2.

lessons.title: Looping Lists
lessons.content: Loop through a list to use each item, like printing each number.

lessons.title: Indentation in Loops
lessons.content: Indent code inside a loop to show it repeats, using 4 spaces.

lessons.question: What keyword starts a for loop?

lessons.title: Loop Magic
lessons.content: Loops save time by repeating tasks automatically.

lessons.title: Loop Leader! 🔄
lessons.content: You’re repeating code like a pro! Loops make your programs efficient and cool!

lessons.title: What are Functions?
lessons.content: Functions are reusable code blocks, like a recipe you can use anytime.

lessons.title: Defining Functions
lessons.content: Use def to create a function, like def say_hi(): print('Hi').

lessons.title: Define a function say_hello() that prints 'Hello' and call it.
Calling Functions
lessons.content: Run a function by using its name with (), like say_hi().

lessons.question: How do you call a function named fun?

lessons.title: Function Structure
lessons.content: A function has a name, () for parameters, and indented code.

lessons.title: Define a function greet() that prints 'Hi there' and call it.
Reusing Functions
lessons.content: Call a function multiple times to reuse its code easily.

lessons.title: Function Power
lessons.content: Functions make your code organized and reusable for big projects.

lessons.title: Function Fanatic! ⚙️
lessons.content: You’re creating reusable code! Functions are your tools for awesome programs!
